answer: Pay a claim only after a licensed assayer tests the claimant's own ground. Each head must present a core cut from a shale ledge it alone holds the lease on; the assayer assays it for ferrous content in person and destroys the core, signing one certificate per epoch. The scarce per-head input is that ground - distinct leases, distinct rock, unprintable and unlendable between heads. A farm's tenth head needs a tenth lease and a tenth core; the assay ledger ties one operator to many sites and the landlords see it, so they refuse, and the marginal head pays rent for ground it can never assay.
